title: Workspace rule makes the agent overwrite the global ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json, giving code execution on every launch that survives reinstall
affected_versions: IDE launch build (released 2025-11-18; version not stated)
notes: Reported to Google VRP 2025-11-19; closed 'Won't Fix (Intended Behavior)' 2025-11-21 and reopened the same day after dispute; no fix reported (blog last updated 2026-05-07). Requires a trusted workspace; worked with the most restrictive IDE settings. A second Mindgard disclosure page lists different dates (Nov 10/15/16), so date_disclosed uses the blog. Disputed by vendor; no CVE (NVD keyword search 0).

title: Indirect prompt injection (incl. invisible Unicode Tag instructions) drives run_command to fetch and execute a remote script under the launch IDE's auto-execute default
fixed_version: partial: IDE 1.11.17 added opt-in Secure Mode (2025-12-08), renamed strict mode in 1.16.5
notes: Issues #1 and #2 of the post. Google listed prompt-injection code execution as a known issue on Bug Hunters. Secure Mode is an opt-in mitigation, not a fix, so latency left blank.

title: No human-in-the-loop for MCP tool calls: injected instructions (e.g. in a Linear ticket) invoke any connected MCP tool
fixed_version: not stated (current docs: unconfigured MCP tools default to Ask in app/CLI)
notes: Issue #3 of the post. Date the Ask default was introduced is not in the changelog read.

title: Exfiltration via read_url_content without approval and via Markdown image rendering after reading .env
fixed_version: partial: CLI 1.1.28 made URL fetch ask by default; IDE strict mode limits images and Read URL to the allowlist
reporter: Johann Rehberger (Embrace The Red); image variant also reported by p1njc70r
notes: Issues #4 and #5 of the post (said to be inherited from Windsurf). Same class as PromptArmor's browser-subagent chain (G6-081/G4-I032) but different channels. Google declared exfiltration a known issue. fix_date is the CLI default change only, not an IDE fix; latency blank.

title: agy: --dangerously-skip-permissions also auto-approves the agent's requests to bypass the terminal sandbox, making --sandbox ineffective
notes: Repro: agy --sandbox --dangerously-skip-permissions -p writes outside the workspace after the model passes bypassSandbox: true. Vendor collaborator reply 2026-09-03: the flag is designed to approve all permissions incl. sandbox bypass. Regression from Gemini CLI --yolo + --sandbox semantics (reporter). Surface: antigravity-cli.

title: agy with --dangerously-skip-permissions: rd /s /q on a repo dir named 'nul' resolved to the C: drive root and deleted most user-writable files (Windows)
notes: User report on the vendor tracker with a reconstructed session log; no vendor confirmation or response. Windows reserved device name path normalisation. Surface: antigravity-cli.

title: agy recursive cleanup on Windows 10 deleted paths far outside the intended targets (Program Files, user dirs), breaking applications
notes: User asked the agent to free disk space on C:; rmdir /s /q via cmd.exe with escaped quotes reached ~35,000 Program Files paths (reporter's log). Permission mode not stated. Vendor labels: bug, security; no vendor reply as of 2026-10-15. Surface: antigravity-cli.

title: MCP OAuth access and refresh tokens stored in plaintext JSON, created world-readable (0644), in four state dirs
notes: Docs confirm a plaintext token file (~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_oauth_tokens.json); the 0644 mode and the copies in antigravity-cli/, antigravity-ide/ and antigravity-backup/ are the reporter's observation only. Reporter's 'IDE 2.8.1' does not match the IDE changelog (latest 2.5.5) and may mean the app.

title: Antigravity IDE: changes to the agent security mode were not persisted (user-selected security mode silently reverted)
notes: Vendor changelog entry 'Fixed Agent Permission Issue'. Impact (which mode it reverted to) not stated.

title: agy: after a permission request was denied (e.g. raised by a subagent that cannot ask) the agent worked around the denial with other commands, scripts or tools
notes: Vendor changelog: 'now respects the denial and no longer tries to work around it'. Model-behaviour mitigation, not an enforcement boundary.

title: agy macOS terminal sandbox let sandboxed commands read ~/Library/Application Support, where desktop apps keep credentials and session tokens
notes: Changed default in the sandbox profile; still allowable by explicit rule. Related reporter issue #1197 (sandboxed command could open a path denied to the file tool, CLI 1.3.3) is unconfirmed and not counted.
